intended_use: A check of the method on public data with real outcomes. This model is not for scoring anyone: it shows how the same pipeline does where the outcomes are known.

metrics.measured_on: validation period (the held-back test period is not used here)
metrics.split: at random, keeping the same share of repaid loans in each part
metrics.split_note: Weaker split: this data source has no usable dates, so loans were divided at random (keeping the same share of repaid loans in each part) instead of by time.
metrics.calibration: none (the model's probabilities were already well calibrated)
metrics.inputs: Share of the instalments on earlier loans paid on or before the due day | Share of the instalments on earlier loans paid more than 30 days late, or still unpaid after 30 days | Share of the instalments on earlier loans where less than 99% of the amount due was paid | The on-time share over instalments due in the 365 days before the application | Share of the monthly records of earlier store and cash loans with an amount overdue | The loan's repayment amount divided by the income stated in the application | The loan amount divided by the price of the goods it pays for | Average of the scores "from external data sources" that the application has (up to three)
metrics.simpler_model: the applicant's own repayment behaviour and loan terms, without the outside score
metrics.data_source: Home Credit Default Risk (Kaggle, 2018), a sample of applicants; the publisher does not state the country
metrics.terms: Kaggle competition rules limit use to that competition and forbid redistribution; used here only as a local, non-commercial method check, by the team lead's decision. Rows are never shown; only totals
metrics.label: Repaid: the applicant had no payment difficulties
metrics.banner: Public data: Home Credit (country not stated), not ShopUp data. Decision support only.
metrics.what_this_shows: Most of the ranking comes from a credit score bought from outside; the applicant's own instalment history and loan terms carry little.
metrics.what_this_does_not_show: That repayment history alone is enough on this data, or anything about Asia: the country is not stated.
metrics.group_findings: Ranking differs for age band 'under 30' (1,170 loans): AUC 0.67 against 0.75 for everyone else. Ranking differs for region rating '2' (6,207 loans): AUC 0.73 against 0.80 for everyone else.

limitations: Public data, not ShopUp data; the country is not stated, so it carries no claim about Asia. The split is random because the source has no calendar dates.
Individual rows are never shown on any screen: the competition rules forbid redistribution. Only totals like these appear.
Labels exist only for people who received credit before. The model may not work for applicants who would have been turned down under earlier policy.
Scores are less certain when coverage is low. A thin file is never treated as a bad file: below the coverage line the band is 'Needs more info', whatever the score.
The numbers above are from the validation period. It was also used to choose the model and the calibration, so they are a little optimistic.
Group columns are used only to audit results, never as model inputs. The group audit shows where the model works measurably differently on these data; it does not show that the model is fair.
The tool supports a human decision. It must not be used for automatic approval or decline.
